record.Description: This recall involves ororo’s rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs, model PD10K-Pro. The black battery packs have a built-in USB-C cable and a digital display. “ororo” is written on the front of the battery pack. The model and a seven alphanumeric serial number starting with 67U, 685, 686 or 68A is printed on the back.
record.Title: Ororo Recalls Rechargeable Lithium-Ion Battery Packs Due to Risk of Serious Injury from Fire and Burn Hazards
record.ConsumerContact: Ororo at 702-751-7639 between 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday, email at recall@ororowear.com, or online at Ororowear.com/pd10k-pro-recall or Ororowear.com and click on “Recall” for more information.

Products.Name: Ororo PD10K-Pro Rechargeable Lithium-Ion Battery Packs
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 269 (In addition, about 24 were sold in Canada)

Images.Caption: Recalled ororo PD10K-Pro Rechargeable Lithium-ion Battery Pack
“PD10K-Pro” and a seven alphanumeric serial number starting with 67U, 685, 686 or 68A is printed on the back of the recalled ororo battery packs.

Injuries.Name: Ororo has received one report of the battery pack overheating. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name:
Sold Online At:
Ororowear.com and Amazon.com from September 2026 through October 2026 for about $109.

Importers.Name: Langis LLC, dba ororo, of Las Vegas, Nevada

Hazards.Name: The recalled lithium-ion battery packs can overheat, posing a risk of serious injury from fire and burn hazards.

Remedies.Name:
Consumers should stop using the battery packs immediately and contact ororo for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to go to Ororowear.com/pd10k-pro-recall to register and to receive disposal instructions. Once registered, consumers should dispose of the recalled battery packs in accordance with local and state regulations.  

Note: Do not throw this recalled lithium-ion battery or device in the trash, the general recycling stream (e.g., street-level or curbside recycling bins), or used battery recycling boxes found at various retail and home improvement stores. Recalled lithium-ion batteries must be disposed of differently than other batteries, because they present a greater risk of fire. Your municipal household hazardous waste (HHW) collection center may accept this recalled lithium-ion battery or device for disposal. Before taking your battery or device to a HHW collection center, contact that office ahead of time and ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, contact your municipality for further guidance.

ai.summary: Ororo has recalled its model PD10K-Pro rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs. The units can overheat, creating fire and burn hazards that could result in serious injuries.
ai.next_steps: Immediately stop using the battery packs and contact Ororo to obtain a full refund. Consumers must register at Ororowear.com/pd10k-pro-recall for disposal directions and follow local and state regulations for proper disposal instead of placing the battery in household trash or standard recycling bins.
